official.tuition_coverage_note: Consortium's published wording: 'The EMJMD scholarships are including student participation costs (including the tuition fees, full insurance coverage and any other mandatory costs related to student participation in the course), a contribution to student travel and installation cost and a subsistence allowance for the entire duration of the EMJMD study programme.' The Erasmus+ Programme Guide confirms that selected projects cannot charge tuition fees or other mandatory costs related to student participation in the course to Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders.

Demonstrated English language proficiency at B2 advanced level, evidenced by an accepted certificate

Second step: a 20-30 minute video-conference interview about motivation and the choice of the second-year study track (weight 25%); only top candidates are interviewed and being interviewed does not mean selection

Eligibility screening by the Bioceb Secretariat: incomplete files and files received after the deadline are eliminated, and non-eligible candidates are informed of the reasons with the possibility to appeal

A contribution to student travel and installation costs
A subsistence allowance for the entire duration of the EMJMD study programme (1 400 Euros per month, maximum 24 months / EUR 33,600)

Compulsory physical mobility for all enrolled students: a minimum of two study periods in two countries different from the student's country of residence at enrolment, each corresponding to at least one academic semester (30 ECTS)

official.citizenship_residency: Erasmus Mundus scholarships are open to students from all over the world, but consortia should ensure geographical balance, i.e. no more than 10% of the total number of scholarships awarded during project implementation should be awarded to candidates from the same nationality
official.international_eligibility: Yes - Erasmus Mundus scholarships are offered to students from all over the world, subject to the geographical-balance rule
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: A BSc or equivalent degree of at least 180 ECTS in engineering or science with a strong background in at least one biology-related discipline (biotechnology, biochemistry, microbiology, biophysics, bioprocess engineering, molecular biology); a complementary background in chemistry, physics or environmental sciences is preferred but non-mandatory
official.description: Bioceb, the European Master in Biological and Chemical Engineering for a Sustainable Bioeconomy, is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master delivered jointly by Aalto University (Finland), AgroParisTech (France), Universite de Liege (Belgium), TalTech (Estonia) and Universite de Reims Champagne Ardenne (France). The consortium states that it recruits up to 26 well-motivated students from all over the world and presents the programme as interdisciplinary training tackling bioeconomy challenges. Bioceb is currently listed in the European Commission's Erasmus Mundus Catalogue.
official.program_type: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degree (EMJM) scholarship
official.english_requirement: B2 advanced English proficiency is required and proof of proficiency is compulsory. Accepted certificates: IELTS Academic overall band 6.5 with 5.5 for Writing; TOEFL iBT overall 92 with 22 for Writing (Home Edition accepted) or TOEFL PDT with Reading 22, Listening 22 and Writing 24; Cambridge C1 Advanced (CAE) grade A, B or C, or C2 Proficiency (CPE) grade A, B, C or Level C1; Pearson Test of English Academic overall 62 with 54 for Writing. A test is not required only if the applicant earned a degree in an English-medium programme (with a university certificate proving this) at a higher education institution of applied sciences in an EU/EEA country, or in an English-speaking country with English as its official language.

applicant_utility.summary: Bioceb is a two-year, five-university Erasmus Mundus master that pays EUR 1,400 a month for up to 24 months (an EUR 33,600 ceiling) and bars the consortium from charging scholarship holders any participation costs, so tuition, insurance and mandatory fees stay off your bill. The real risks are timing and evidence: the consortium states the programme is not running in 2025-2027 and points to the 2026-2028 campaign, and the official application platform showed no open campaign yet, so keep a funded alternative for 2027 open. One file decides both admission and the scholarship, and the two most common ways to lose it before anyone reads your transcripts are referees who never upload their letters and untranslated documents. The published selection weights make this unusually transparent - excellence at 35% and motivation at 20% mean your letter must do real argumentative work, not just praise your grades.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Engineering or science graduates with a strong, named biology specialisation (biotechnology, biochemistry, microbiology, biophysics, bioprocess or molecular biology) who want two years across Finland, France, Belgium or Estonia with tuition and living costs covered.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your BSc is at least 180 ECTS and decide which biology-related discipline is your strength, because the published minimum is discipline-specific rather than a generic 'BSc required'
Secure two referees early and verify they receive and act on the platform request, since referees upload their own letters and you cannot attach them on their behalf
Collect signed, stamped transcripts for every year of the BSc with a grading-system explanation, and commission official English translations before the window opens

Book an accepted English test early - IELTS Academic 6.5 (5.5 writing), TOEFL iBT 92 (22 writing), TOEFL PDT 22/22/24, Cambridge C1 Advanced A-C or C2 Proficiency A-C1, or PTE Academic 62 (54 writing) - unless you qualify for the English-medium degree exemption
Obtain a proof of place of residence issued in English and dated within the last 12 months, since it is on the required document list and is easy to overlook
common_rejection_risks: An incomplete file: the Secretariat states incomplete applications will not be taken into consideration, so one missing translation removes you before any academic assessment
Referees missing the platform deadline - the letters are theirs to upload, and a late letter leaves the file formally incomplete
Forgetting the final validation step in the application tool: only validated applications are considered

A biology-adjacent BSc that does not meet the published minimum, which requires a strong background in biotechnology, biochemistry, microbiology, biophysics, bioprocess engineering or molecular biology

Nationality crowding: with a hard cap of 10% of all project scholarships per nationality, a competitive application from a heavily represented country can rank below a weaker file from an under-represented one
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The EUR 1,400 monthly allowance has to stretch across travel, visa, installation and subsistence for the whole programme, so the first housing deposit, local transport, study materials and personal spending all come out of that same envelope before any payment arrives.
document_audit: Referees upload their own letters through the platform; the Bioceb reference-letter form is published as a PDF on the official site and should be sent to them
Every non-English diploma and transcript needs an official English translation attached to the same file; French, German and Dutch are the stated exception for the high-school diploma
An ID copy is accepted only for European students; everyone else must upload a passport scan showing photo, expiry date and personal details
The proof of place of residence must be issued in English or officially translated and dated no more than 12 months before application
alerts: The consortium has publicly stated the programme will not run in 2025-2027 and that the next round is the 2026-2028 campaign; the official application platform showed no open campaign at verification time, so confirm the exact window before making plans
Results are announced in April, which is late for most fellowship, housing and visa planning - line up a parallel application
The scholarship cannot be stacked with a previous Erasmus Mundus award, so a former EMJMD or EMJM scholarship holder is permanently excluded
The allowance is pro-rated to the actual days of study, research, placement and thesis defence, so a longer programme does not automatically mean more months of support
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create an account on the official AgroParisTech eMundus tool, upload the full document set including translations, have both referees submit their letters, then validate the submission; the Secretariat screens completeness and eligibility before any academic ranking is applied.

official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording: 'Please note that tuition fees are not covered by the scholarship.' The rulebook adds that scholarship holders are exempt from tuition fees at public higher education institutions that apply the standard national tuition rates for non-European students, and that France Excellence status carries a conditional exemption from registration fees for programmes offered by public universities under the supervision of the French Ministry of Higher Education and Research, provided that no additional tuition fees apply.
benefits: France Excellence scholarship holder status, which carries social security coverage and health insurance for the whole stay in France, support services from Campus France Paris, exemption from visa fees and exemption from the Student and Campus Life Contribution (CVEC)
A monthly living allowance of 900 EUR per month for Master's students and 1,850 EUR per month for PhD students, subject to reassessment
One return flight ticket between the recipient's country of residence and France

Priority access to student housing in CROUS student residences, plus eligibility to apply for additional housing support from the French Family Allowance Fund (CAF) of approximately 150 EUR per month depending on individual circumstances

Conditional exemption from registration fees for programmes offered by public universities under the supervision of the French Ministry of Higher Education and Research, provided that no additional tuition fees apply
eligibility: Be a citizen of South Africa, Lesotho or Malawi
Be born on or after 1 January 1997
Not be a dual French citizen
Have achieved a minimum average of 60% in the most recently completed degree

Master's applicants: plan to enrol in a Master's degree at a French higher education institution; admission is not required at the time of application, and final-year Bachelor's or Honours students may apply with proof of current enrolment and most recent transcripts
PhD applicants: plan to pursue a PhD at a French higher education institution and have identified a prospective supervisor or research laboratory in France

Incomplete applications, or applications which fail to meet the deadline, will be automatically rejected
Applicants must not initiate follow-up enquiries regarding the status of their application

An up-to-date CV that also states the candidate's entire academic history, and a cover letter explaining motivations and interests in the planned academic project
Copies of all previous academic degree certificates, and university transcripts (academic marks) of at least three years of studies

Optional: a cost-sharing commitment letter from the corresponding organisation, academic and/or professional recommendations, and language proficiency certificates (French TCF, DELF, DALF)

The quality and coherence of the study project with the candidate's background, and the clarity and quality of future career plans
For PhD applicants, PhDs under co-supervision are favoured and the commitment of South African and French supervisors is decisive
The level of proficiency in foreign languages and its adequacy with the chosen study programmes; the programme states all criteria carry equal importance in the overall evaluation
Shortlisted candidates are interviewed before the Advisory Board identifies grant recipients; applicants are shortlisted on the basis of the quality of their file

At least 60% of scholarships are allocated to priority fields (STEM and related humanities and social sciences); the remainder go to other fields; there is no specific quota on the number of scholarships granted

One return economy-class airfare between the recipient's country of residence and France
Social security coverage and health insurance for the whole stay in France
Priority access to student housing, exemption from visa fees and exemption from the CVEC

official.citizenship_residency: Restricted to citizens of South Africa, Lesotho and Malawi; dual French citizens are not eligible.
official.international_eligibility: No - the programme is limited to citizens of South Africa, Lesotho and Malawi.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All fields of study are eligible, with priority given to digital technologies, artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, biotechnology, health, environmental sciences, energy, low-carbon mobility, space, food systems and information and communication technologies, including related humanities and social sciences; at least 60% of scholarships go to these priority fields.
official.research_requirement: PhD applicants must submit a detailed research project description of 2-3 pages including a work plan, and a supervisor commitment letter; for co-supervision (cotutelle) the letter must confirm enrolment at both universities and award of the degree by the French institution, with a schedule of periods to be spent in France.
official.duration: Master's: the duration of the degree, with Master's programmes stated to be two years long, and continued funding conditional on the Embassy verifying academic success at the end of the first year; PhD: a maximum of 3 years, renewed each academic year on justified research progress; funding covers only the period of study and research undertaken in France
official.description: The Embassy of France in South Africa runs this highly selective France Excellence call so that citizens of South Africa, Lesotho and Malawi can study for a Master's or PhD at a French higher education institution, aiming to strengthen high-level exchanges between France and South Africa. Laureates receive a monthly living allowance, a return flight, social security and health insurance, housing priority and fee exemptions, but not tuition. Because the hemispheres' calendars oppose, they follow online French-language courses through the Alliances Francaises network from February to July 2027 before departing for France in September 2027.
official.region: Africa (South Africa, Lesotho, Malawi); study takes place in France

applicant_utility.summary: This Embassy of France award pays EUR 900 a month for a Master's and EUR 1,850 for a PhD plus a return flight, insurance, housing priority and fee exemptions, but it deliberately leaves tuition to you, so a public-university programme at national rates is the only version of this scholarship that closes the budget. The opposing hemispheres force laureates into online Alliance Francaise French courses from February to July and a September departure, which effectively maps out your whole gap year between winning and arriving. With at least 60% of awards earmarked for STEM and the listed priority fields, a science or technology project has a structural advantage, and nothing converts a shortlist place into money until a French institution actually admits you. The 2027 call closed on 8 October 2026, so the actionable move now is to build the file for the June 2027 call.
applicant_utility.best_fit: South African, Lesothoan or Malawian citizens born in or after 1997 with 60%-plus averages and a concrete Master's or PhD project at a French institution, especially in STEM or a listed priority field.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist up to three Master's programmes with webpage links, application deadlines and tuition fees, ranked in order of preference
For a PhD, secure the supervisor commitment letter before applying and draft the 2-3 page research project with a work plan
Gather degree certificates and transcripts covering at least three years of study, and a CV that states the entire academic history
Save email exchanges with the French institutions as evidence of contact, since formal admission is not required at application

Verify the chosen programme is a qualification recognised by the French Ministry of Higher Education and Research, since many programmes labelled MSc are not nationally recognised Master's degrees in France
common_rejection_risks: Forgetting the mandatory 'final submission' step - an unsubmitted, incomplete or late file is automatically rejected
Choosing a specialised or private programme whose fees exceed standard national rates, which leaves tuition entirely uncovered
A study project that reads as disconnected from previous studies, or with vague future career plans
Tripping a hard gate - age (born on or after 1 January 1997), citizenship, dual French citizenship or the 60% average - which makes the file non-eligible on sight
Assuming a scholarship application guarantees enrolment; French institutions decide admission alone and awards are only finalised once admission is secured
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees and any differentiated registration fees at non-public or specialised programmes, plus day-to-day overspend beyond the EUR 900 or EUR 1,850 monthly allowance and the Etudes en France procedure fee at first (reimbursed to laureates).
document_audit: An ID copy is acceptable instead of a passport at application, but a valid passport is essential by May for travel and administrative procedures
Transcripts must cover at least three years of studies, and the CV must state the entire academic history
PhD supervisor letters must spell out cotutelle details where applicable, including which institution awards the degree
Recommendation letters, cost-sharing letters and language certificates are optional - do not let optional extras crowd out the mandatory core file
alerts: The 8 October 2026 23:59 (SA time) deadline has already passed; the next call is expected in June 2027 for September 2028 entry, and a scholarship cannot be deferred to another year

Winning the scholarship does not guarantee admission - the final award depends on acceptance into a French programme, with proof due between February and July 2027 and final awards confirmed in four waves from May to July 2027
Participation in the February-July online French courses is highly encouraged and is taken into account for the final awarding of the scholarship
The scholarship can be ended at any time if the laureate does not fulfil study requirements, and the programme is explicitly not intended for individuals seeking immigration opportunities
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the programme website, complete the online form and upload the document set, press 'final submission' before the closing date; shortlisted candidates are interviewed in November, shortlists are announced from early December and all contact is made individually.
